data.title: Tesla FSD Records Nearly 10 Times Fewer Crashes in Belgium
data.description:
Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) has recorded a significantly lower collision rate than human-driven Teslas since the system was approved in Belgium this summer, according to new figures presented to the Flemish Parliament.

Flemish Mobility Minister Annick De Ridder shared the results on Thursday. The data, supplied by Tesla as part of the conditions attached to its Belgian approval, covers driving between June 11 and August 31.

Over that period, Tesla vehicles travelled 24.6 million km with FSD engaged. The largest difference was recorded away from highways, where there was one collision across 9.5 million km of assisted driving.

By comparison, manually driven Teslas were involved in 150 collisions over 146.9 million km. Based on those figures, the collision risk was approximately 9.6 times lower when FSD was active.

The difference was smaller on highways but still favoured Tesla’s driver-assistance technology. Four incidents occurred during 15.1 million km with FSD engaged, compared with 32 incidents across 95.1 million km under manual control. That works out to an improvement of roughly 30 percent.

Five accidents involving participating vehicles were reported to the Flemish administration. FSD was inactive in one, although the driver had disengaged it prematurely while exiting a roundabout. Investigators reportedly found no link between FSD and the other four accidents – all were minor, low-speed collisions without injuries. (via HLN)

Tesla’s data also showed 93 percent fewer automatic emergency braking activations and between 82 and 90 percent fewer abrupt manoeuvres, including hard braking and sharp steering inputs.

The figures add to Tesla’s growing European dataset, which was made public earlier this month, as regulators prepare for a broader EU decision on the technology on October 6.

“New technology deserves critical follow-up, but if the data shows that it can make our roads safer, we must also dare to use that potential,” De Ridder said. “It turns out that road safety and innovation can go hand in hand.”

Before receiving approval in June, Tesla completed 5,000 km of testing on Belgian roads in roughly one month. The testing evaluated how FSD responds to infrastructure and driving conditions specific to Belgium, including tram networks, bicycle streets, advisory bike lanes, supplemental signage, and temporary traffic controls in construction zones.

FSD is already approved in five European countries – the Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Estonia, and Lithuania – where more than 70,000 customers are using it for over one million km each day.

data.title: Tesla Optimus Factory Build Accelerates Ahead Of 2027 Production Target
data.description:
New drone footage from Giga Texas shows Tesla’s dedicated Optimus factory taking shape, with the building’s steel structure nearing completion as construction continues on the company’s massive North Campus expansion.

Drone operator Joe Tegtmeyer shared updated aerial views of the site on September 17, showing the Optimus building’s steel frame approaching the final stages of assembly. According to Teslarati, the structure is now roughly five column grids away from reaching the north perimeter beam.

Concrete work is also progressing, with three upper floors already poured while crews continue installing rebar and completing footing and grade-beam work below.

Tesla broke ground on the dedicated Optimus facility in late March, with the first steel installed in May after the company confirmed construction was underway. The building is part of a larger expansion of more than 5.2 million square feet on the north side of the Texas factory campus.

The future Optimus facility is expected to stretch more than 4,000 feet alongside the existing vehicle factory, although it will be narrower in design.

Tesla has previously outlined ambitious plans for Optimus, with CEO Elon Musk targeting eventual production capacity of up to 10 million units annually at full scale. A separate pilot production line at Fremont has reportedly been producing Gen 3 Optimus units since January, with output focused on collecting real-world data ahead of future larger-scale manufacturing.

As we reported earlier this year, Tesla’s Texas Optimus facility is being built alongside other major projects, including the company’s planned Terafab chip manufacturing operation with SpaceX. The co-location is intended to bring key parts of Tesla’s future AI and robotics supply chain closer together.

Tesla has not announced production has started at the Texas Optimus factory. The company’s previously stated timeline targets high-volume Optimus production at Giga Texas in summer 2027, once construction and additional manufacturing infrastructure are complete.

data.title: IMC Logistics adds 50 Tesla Semis to California fleet
data.description:
Tesla has landed another significant Semi order, with IMC Logistics announcing plans to add 50 of the electric Class 8 trucks to its fleet in California.

IMC Logistics describes itself as the largest asset-based marine drayage operator in North America, with more than 2,700 trucks and over 50 locations across the continent. The company confirmed the Tesla Semi deployment this week during the 2026 Intermodal EXPO in Long Beach, where it already had one of its trucks on display.

The order will include a mix of Standard and Long Range Tesla Semis. IMC plans to use the Standard Range version, with a range of 325 miles (523 km) for drayage operations within California, while the Long Range trucks will travel between Southern California and destinations farther inland with its range of up to 500 miles (804 km).

The company did not announce how many of each variant it purchased.

The Tesla Semis won’t be IMC’s first alternative-fuel trucks. The company already operates battery-electric and hydrogen fuel-cell trucks in California, along with trucks powered by renewable diesel. IMC says using several technologies allows it to match different trucks with specific routes and customer requirements.

“We are focused on making sustainability attainable in day-to-day drayage operations,” said Jim Gillis, Pacific Region President at IMC Logistics. “That means taking a blended approach rather than relying on a single technology. The addition of 50 Tesla Semis strengthens that strategy as well as allows IMC to establish zero-emission service for long haul lanes.”

The deal adds to a growing order book for the Tesla Semi as the company ramps up production at its new high-volume factory in Nevada.

Earlier this year, WattEV announced an order for 370 Tesla Semis in a deal worth nearly US$100 million. That record was recently surpassed by Swedish transport company Einride, which last month announced plans to purchase 500 Tesla Semis for its U.S. operations.

Tesla is also preparing to expand the Semi beyond North America. The company recently unveiled its European version of the truck, which offers up to 550 km (342 miles) of range, ahead of planned European deliveries in 2027.

data.title: Tesla raises Wall Connector prices again in Canada, Universal model nears $1,000
data.description:
Tesla has once again raised the price of its home charging equipment in Canada, continuing a string of increases this year that have made the Wall Connector significantly more expensive.

According to an update to the Tesla Shop listing this week, the standard Wall Connector is now listed for $815. That’s another $55 increase from the $760 price we reported previously.

While the July price increases were limited to the standard Wall Connector, narrowing the gap between the two chargers to just $40, Tesla has now raised the price of the Universal Wall Connector as well. It is now listed at $945, up from $800 in July and $875 last month, widening the gap between the two models to $130.

Unlike the standard model, the Universal Wall Connector includes an integrated J1772 adapter, allowing it to charge both NACS-equipped vehicles and EVs using the J1772 connector.

The latest adjustment continues a run of price increases for the standard Wall Connector. Earlier this summer, the charger could be purchased for $630, before Tesla raised it to $645, then $675 and $760. At $815, it is now $185 more expensive than it was in early June, an increase of more than 29% in just over three months.

But that is only the past three months. The Wall Connector has previously sold for as little as $465 in Canada. Compared with that price, Canadians are now paying $350 more, or roughly 75% more.

The increases weren’t limited to Canada. In the U.S., the standard Wall Connector is now $585 (was $535) and the Universal Wall Connector is priced at $660 (was $600).

Tesla has not provided an explanation for the latest increases, but despite the higher prices, the Wall Connector is still one of the most reliable home chargers you can buy.

data.title: Tesla Q3 Delivery Forecast Cut to 435,000 by Goldman Sachs
data.description:
Goldman Sachs has lowered its forecast for Tesla’s third quarter deliveries, citing weaker-than-expected sales in several of the automaker’s largest markets.

The investment bank now expects Tesla to deliver 435,000 vehicles globally during Q3, down from its previous estimate of 490,000. The revised figure is also well below the consensus estimate of approximately 456,000 vehicles.

If Goldman’s forecast proves accurate, Tesla deliveries would fall by roughly 9% compared to the second quarter. Tesla delivered 480,126 vehicles in Q2, including 467,762 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, rebounding significantly from 358,023 deliveries during the first three months of the year.

According to Goldman, recent sales figures from the U.S., China and Europe have been tracking below its previous expectations. Stronger demand in export markets, including Southeast Asia, South America and Australia, is expected to partly offset that weakness, with many of those vehicles being exported from Giga Shanghai.

Despite lowering its delivery estimate, Goldman has maintained its Neutral rating on Tesla and its $360 price target. Analyst Mark Delaney reiterated both earlier this week, while pointing to a few areas that could provide some upside to vehicle demand.

Among them is Full Self-Driving (FSD), which Delaney believes could help support demand. Goldman also sees the larger six-seat Model Y L as another potential contributor to improving sales over time. U.S. deliveries of the Model Y L are expected to begin later this month.

Goldman did not provide a Canada specific Q3 forecast. Tesla is expected to release its official third quarter production and delivery figures in early October.

data.title: Tesla adding more public Semi Megachargers with Forum Mobility
data.description:
Tesla’s Semi Megacharger network is getting another major boost, with Forum Mobility preparing to break ground on four new heavy-duty electric truck charging depots in California.

According to Forum Mobility, the four facilities will add approximately 30 MW of charging capacity across Northern and Southern California, with both traditional CCS chargers and the newer Megawatt Charging System (MCS).

Tesla will have a direct role at three of the new locations, operating public Megacharging at Forum Mobility locations in Ontario and Oakland. All three will be public and open to commercial carriers, rather than being reserved exclusively for Tesla’s own Semi fleets.

The fourth site will be in Santa Fe, New Mexico, which already has contracted fleet offtake covering more than 330 Tesla Semis. Despite that commitment, Forum says public charging access will remain available to other commercial operators.

The new depots will feature pull-through MCS lanes, allowing trucks to charge without disconnecting their trailers. According to Forum, MCS hardware can add up to approximately 60% of a truck’s range in about 30 minutes.

Forum is also expanding its existing Megacharger infrastructure at their depot at the Port of Long Beach. That facility has been operational since December 2024 with 44 CCS ports and 9 MW of capacity, and has now received two Tesla Megachargers.

While the network is growing in the U.S., it may soon be coming to Canada. As Drive Tesla previously reported, Tesla has been planning a Canadian Semi Megacharger rollout along Ontario’s Highway 401 corridor, laying the groundwork for the Semi’s eventual arrival north of the border.

Tesla has also been working to speed up deployments with pre-assembled Megacharger stations, which arrive largely assembled and can significantly reduce on-site construction work.

data.title: Another Tesla driver caught “sound asleep” behind the wheel in B.C.
data.description:
Apparently five incidents weren’t enough. Police in British Columbia have reported yet another case involving a driver allegedly sleeping behind the wheel of a Tesla with driver-assist features engaged.

The latest incident happened in Port Coquitlam, where the Coquitlam RCMP received a report last week of a driver who appeared to be asleep behind the wheel of a Model Y travelling with Autopilot engaged. [The press release says Autopilot, but we assume it was actually Full Self-Driving (FSD).]

The Integrated Road Safety Unit (IRSU) was called in to assist and managed to locate the vehicle, where officers found the driver was “sound asleep” behind the wheel.

Making matters worse, the driver was also still in B.C.’s graduated licensing program, holding a Class 7 Novice, or “N,” licence.

Police stopped the vehicle and issued the driver a ticket for driving without due care and attention, along with a second violation ticket for failing to display the required “N” sign.

“Drivers of all vehicles must be in control at all times when automated features are engaged while operating a motor vehicle in British Columbia,” Coquitlam RCMP said.

The Port Coquitlam incident adds to an unusual string of similar cases involving Tesla drivers in B.C. this year.

In March, a Model Y driver was ticketed after allegedly appearing asleep on Highway 1 in Coquitlam. Since then, drivers have been caught or reported allegedly sleeping behind the wheel in North Vancouver, Langley and between Golden and Revelstoke. Another Tesla driver was ticketed in West Kelowna after police spotted them reading documents while driving with FSD engaged.

The incidents have even attracted attention south of the border. Last week, U.S. Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi called on federal regulators to investigate safeguards surrounding Tesla’s Autopilot and FSD after an investigation identified 43 online videos that appeared to show people asleep behind the wheel of moving Teslas. It was unclear if any of those videos were of Canadian drivers.

data.title: Lucid And Bolt Plan 25,000 Autonomous Vehicles Across Europe
data.description:
Lucid is making another major move into the robotaxi market, this time partnering with European mobility company Bolt on plans to deploy at least 25,000 fully autonomous electric vehicles across Europe.

According to Lucid, the vehicles will be based on its upcoming Midsize platform and developed for SAE Level 4 autonomous operation. The platform is expected to use NVIDIA Hyperion, which combines the computing hardware and sensor suite.

Bolt Autonomous Driving Solutions will lead the program on Bolt’s side, while the recently formed Lucid Technologies unit will oversee Lucid’s involvement. Bolt intends to own and operate the vehicles, while also developing the fleet infrastructure, operating systems and city partnerships required to put them into service.

“Autonomous driving in Europe requires data, software, vehicles, and operations to work as one system built for European roads and regulation,” Bolt founder and CEO Markus Villig said.

Neither company has provided a timeline for when the first vehicles will enter service.

This isn’t Lucid’s first major robotaxi deal. In July 2025, the automaker partnered with Uber and Nuro on a separate program involving at least 20,000 Lucid Gravity vehicles. Under that arrangement, Lucid supplies and engineers the vehicle platform while Nuro provides the Level 4 autonomous driving system.

data.title: Tesla launches Model Y L accessories in the US ahead of first deliveries
data.description:
Tesla is preparing to deliver the first Model Y L vehicles in the United States in the coming weeks, and ahead of those deliveries has launched a collection of accessories designed specifically for the larger six-seat SUV.

And in case you’re wondering, no similar shop has been added in Canada as Canadian buyers are still waiting for their chance to order the extended wheelbase Model Y L.

Among the new products are Model Y L-specific all-weather interior, trunk and seatback liners, along with front, roof and rear liftgate sunshades. Tesla is also selling rear door sill guards for US$95 and a pair of moulded trunk storage bins for US$80.

Tesla has also launched a Model Y L roof rack for US$500, rated to carry up to 165 lbs (75 kg). A fitted outdoor car cover is US$195, while a parcel shelf for behind the third row is US$125.

Not everything we expected to see in the Model Y L shop has made an appearance, however. Compared to China, where the SUV has been available since last year, the US lineup is still missing a few accessories, including privacy shades for the side windows and the Model Y L air mattress.

Owners won’t necessarily need Model Y L-specific versions of every accessory. Several products designed for the regular Model Y are cross-compatible, including frunk bins, console organizers and other smaller items. Tesla’s vehicle-to-load (V2L) adapter also works with both vehicles.

As we noted above, while US deliveries are about to begin, Tesla has yet to offer the Model Y L to Canadian buyers. Its absence is somewhat surprising given that Tesla has been importing Model 3s from Giga Shanghai into Canada since earlier this year, meaning the company already has an established supply route from China.

Despite that, the China-built Model Y L is still missing from Tesla’s Canadian online configurator. Tesla currently imports the Model Y into Canada from Giga Berlin in Germany, while US customers will receive Model Y Ls built at Giga Texas.

data.title: Tesla Expands Forecasted Supercharger Availability to Android Auto
data.description:
Tesla is expanding one of its more useful Supercharger planning features, with forecasted stall availability now also available through Android Auto.

The expansion comes after Tesla Charging announced in June that forecasted Supercharger availability was rolling out globally to EVs with Google Maps built-in. The feature gives drivers an estimate of how many Supercharger stalls will be available when they arrive, rather than simply showing how many are free at the moment.

Now Tesla says the same capability is available through Android Auto, significantly increasing the number of EVs that can take advantage of the technology.

Going Beyond Live Availability

The expansion follows Tesla’s recent addition of live Supercharger availability to Google Maps in Canada and the United States. That integration allows EV drivers to see the current number of available stalls at a Supercharger without using Tesla’s app or in-car navigation.

Forecasted availability takes that a step further. Instead of showing only what is happening at a station right now, the system attempts to predict conditions when the driver actually reaches the Supercharger.

Drivers with eligible EVs can opt in to the feature, which also allows their navigation data to help improve Tesla’s charging forecasts.
